entries.title: Compact find_callers answers (#52)
entries.summary: The Markdown answer of the MCP tool and of knot callers --output markdown keeps every count but lists only what an agent needs.
highlights: Compact find_callers answers (#52). The Markdown answer of the MCP tool and of knot callers --output markdown keeps every count but lists only what an agent needs. References made from test code (test files, Rust #[cfg(test)]) are counted and not listed: each group ends with +N in tests, and the Found line states how many there are. A single-repository answer names its repository once, on the Found line, as (repo: name), while a multi-repository answer still labels every row. Rows are one line each, with the signature on that line when it is not empty, and a file's <module> row (its import) is folded into the file's other rows. Row shape is unchanged (- \name\ (kind) at \path:line\``) and so is the JSON output, which lists every row.
include_tests parameter on find_callers (CLI --include-tests) lists the references made from test code.

Reference rows now carry is_test_context, so the search summaries of #50 count Rust #[cfg(test)] callers as test code. The reference queries did not return the flag before, so those callers were reported as production callers. JSON rows gain the is_test_context field.

Token-efficiency benchmark re-run on today's snapshots (spring-ai b6b5767, puppeteer 08e7b1a, knot 421b515): 87.4% fewer tokens (≈7.9×) across the nine tasks, against 76.1% with v1.14.1 and 73.5% with v1.12.4 on the same snapshots. The callers rows went from 29 772 to 4 372 tokens. Listing test references too brings the total to 80.4%. The raw measurements now record the knot version and the snapshot commits.

entries.title: HTTP client links are relinked in one serialized transaction (#46)
entries.summary: Every indexer run replaced all HTTP_CALLS edges in two separate statements after reading its inputs outside any transaction, so two runs finishing together (knot-server cluster nodes sharing Neo4j)…
highlights: HTTP client links are relinked in one serialized transaction (#46). Every indexer run replaced all HTTP_CALLS edges in two separate statements after reading its inputs outside any transaction, so two runs finishing together (knot-server cluster nodes sharing Neo4j) could leave the edges missing for a moment, or keep a set computed from a stale snapshot until the next run. The relink pass (repository facts, inputs, delete, create) now runs in one transaction that first locks the singleton :HttpCallsLock node, unique by a new constraint created at startup. A concurrent pass waits until it commits, so the last pass sees every committed repository and readers never see the edges half replaced. A failed pass is rolled back and retried up to three times.
The subgraph query accepts HTTP_CALLS, so knot-server's graph API can draw client call → endpoint edges.
The HTTP client E2E suite re-indexes its three repositories concurrently with --clean, twice, and checks that the links converge. Unit test for the subgraph relationship allow-list.
No re-index needed.

entries.title: HTTP client calls are linked to the endpoints they hit (#46)
entries.summary: Every routed method of a declarative client — OpenFeign (@FeignClient), MicroProfile REST Client (@RegisterRestClient), Spring HTTP interface (@GetExchange/@HttpExchange) — and every imperative call…
highlights: HTTP client calls are linked to the endpoints they hit (#46). Every routed method of a declarative client — OpenFeign (@FeignClient), MicroProfile REST Client (@RegisterRestClient), Spring HTTP interface (@GetExchange/@HttpExchange) — and every imperative call — RestTemplate (getForObject, postForEntity, exchange(url, HttpMethod.X, …), …), WebClient / RestClient (.get().uri(…), .method(HttpMethod.X).uri(…), uriBuilder lambdas) — becomes an http_client_call entity named <METHOD> <path> with the client's base URL path applied. After every indexer run, HTTP_CALLS edges (heuristic: true) are recomputed across every indexed repository, so the links do not depend on indexing order and need no build dependency between client and server. A call links to the endpoint matching it best: same verb (or ANY), same segments with {variable} wildcards and at least one literal segment, the server's context path optional, the most literal endpoint winning (/items/{id} over /items/export); when the Feign service name or URL host matches a server's spring.application.name / quarkus.application.name, only that server's endpoints are candidates; a tie links nothing.

Base URLs and server facts are read from the repository's application* / bootstrap* .yml|.yaml|.properties and microprofile-config.properties (test sources excluded), even without --include-config-files: Feign url / spring.cloud.openfeign.client.config.<name>.url, quarkus.rest-client.<key>.url, <key>/mp-rest/url, ${prop:default} placeholders, @Value("${…}") fields and constructor parameters, and the server context path (server.servlet.context-path, spring.mvc.servlet.path, quarkus.http.root-path, @ApplicationPath, …). Imperative URLs are evaluated from literals, concatenation, Kotlin templates, constants, URI.create, String.format and UriComponentsBuilder; an unknown leading part stands for scheme and host, an unknown later part for a {variable} segment, and a relative URL takes the base of the file's single baseUrl(…) / rootUri(…) builder call. Imperative calls in test code are skipped.

find_callers on a handler or endpoint lists the client calls under HTTP callers (heuristic: client call → endpoint); explore_file groups a client's calls under HTTP Client Calls; search results count them (HTTP callers N).

One overload is addressable by its parameter list (#37). com.x.Foo.bar(int, int) resolves com.x.Foo.bar with the usual tiers, then keeps the overloads whose declared parameter types match — simple type names, generic arguments compared only when written, arrays and varargs as [] or ..., name: Type for Kotlin/TypeScript. When none matches, the answer lists the declared overloads; the bare FQN labels each overload by its parameter list (### Target: com.x.Foo.bar(int, int)). Query-side only: existing indexes work without a re-index.

entries.title: Compact search answers for LLM agents (#50)
entries.summary: Each relationship summary is a single line whose samples are relative to the result's file — name (same file) in that file, the file name only elsewhere (the full path is one find_callers away) — and…
highlights: Compact search answers for LLM agents (#50). Each relationship summary is a single line whose samples are relative to the result's file — name (same file) in that file, the file name only elsewhere (the full path is one find_callers away) — and that ends with … +N more when the samples are partial. Callers and usages in test code (is_test_path or #[cfg(test)]) stay in the counts, which still match find_callers, but are reported as N in tests and listed only with the new include_tests parameter (CLI --include-tests). Calls: is one line capped at 8 items; signatures print on one line and empty ones (()) are omitted; documentation keeps its first paragraph without @param/@return tags; a result declared in a file already shown refers to the earlier result instead of repeating the path. JSON output gains *_test_count / *_test_samples, and *_samples now holds production rows only.
detail parameter on search_hybrid_context (CLI --detail): full (default) or brief, one line per result — name (kind) — file:line — called by N, calls M. An unknown value is rejected.

explore_file puts the compact signature on the entity line, cuts documentation previews at the first sentence (read across line breaks, at most 200 characters), and groups Imports / Referenced Types by declaring file, names only. Measured on 8 searches and 3 files over 4 repositories: search full answers are 28% shorter, brief answers 82% shorter, explore_file answers 24% shorter.

this.x reads and writes are no longer stored as CALLS edges (#49). A this.<member> that is not the callee of a call becomes a member access: it produces a REFERENCES edge to a field or constant and a CALLS edge only to a method or getter (this.total, app.use(this.handler)). find_callers on a field lists its readers and writers as references, and search Calls: lists no longer fill up with fields. An arrow-function class field passed as app.use(this.handler) now produces REFERENCES instead of CALLS.

entries.title: Upgrade knot to 1.15.0
entries.summary: The find_callers tool of POST /mcp returns compact Markdown answers: references made from test code (test files, Rust #[cfg(test)]) are counted (+N in tests) and listed only with the new…
highlights: Upgrade knot to 1.15.0. The find_callers tool of POST /mcp returns compact Markdown answers: references made from test code (test files, Rust #[cfg(test)]) are counted (+N in tests) and listed only with the new include_tests: true argument, a single-repository answer names its repository once on the Found line, rows are one line each with a compact signature, and a file's <module> import row is folded into its other rows. Counts are unchanged. No re-index needed.
Reference rows carry is_test_context. The JSON of GET /api/repos/:id/callers and GET /api/callers gains the is_test_context field on every row (knot 1.15.0); all rows are still returned.

Token-efficiency table re-measured. 87.4% fewer tokens (≈7.9×) across the nine benchmark tasks with knot 1.15.0, on recorded snapshots of spring-ai, puppeteer and knot. The README now states that the saving is measured on the Markdown answers that POST /mcp serves; the REST routes return the same results as structured JSON, which is larger.

entries.title: Release binaries are built again
entries.summary: dist 0.31 builds Apple Silicon on macos-14, whose runner image GitHub retires on 2026-11-02.
highlights: Release binaries are built again. dist 0.31 builds Apple Silicon on macos-14, whose runner image GitHub retires on 2026-11-02. Its brownout cancelled the aarch64-apple-darwin job, so v0.9.4 and v0.9.5 have no GitHub Release; both are on crates.io and Docker Hub. The Apple Silicon build now runs on macos-15. No code changes since 0.9.5.

entries.title: HTTP_CALLS in the graph API
entries.summary: relationships=HTTP_CALLS draws the heuristic edges from an HTTP client call to the endpoint it hits, possibly in another repository (knot 1.14).
highlights: HTTP_CALLS in the graph API. relationships=HTTP_CALLS draws the heuristic edges from an HTTP client call to the endpoint it hits, possibly in another repository (knot 1.14). The endpoints kind category now includes http_client_call next to http_endpoint, so relationships=HTTP_CALLS,ROUTES_TO&kinds=endpoints,functions follows a client call to the handler that serves it.

Upgrade knot to 1.14.1. knot relinks HTTP_CALLS in one transaction serialized by a lock on a singleton :HttpCallsLock node, unique by a constraint created at startup. Cluster nodes finishing an index run at the same time no longer leave the edges missing or stale, and the subgraph query accepts HTTP_CALLS. No re-index needed.
Both limitations listed in 0.9.4 (graph support for HTTP_CALLS and the cluster relink race) are resolved.

E2E G24: the Feign client fixture tests/fixtures/http_endpoints/ItemsClient.java reaches GET /items/{id} over HTTP_CALLS in the graph, and the handler's callers list it under http_calls. G17 adds HTTP_CALLS to the relationship round-trip; G21 accepts client calls in the endpoints category.

entries.title: Upgrade knot to 1.14.0
entries.summary: Updated the knot dependency from 1.12.2 to 1.14.0.
highlights: Upgrade knot to 1.14.0. Updated the knot dependency from 1.12.2 to 1.14.0. No API code changes were required. Re-index Java, Kotlin, TypeScript and JavaScript repositories to build the HTTP client calls and drop the false edges fixed upstream.

HTTP callers (knot 1.14.0, Java/Kotlin). GET /api/repos/:id/callers, GET /api/callers and the find_callers MCP tool gain an http_calls bucket: the HTTP client calls linked by heuristic HTTP_CALLS edges to the queried endpoint or handler, from any indexed repository. Covered clients are OpenFeign, MicroProfile REST Client, Spring @HttpExchange, RestTemplate, WebClient and RestClient. Each client call is an http_client_call entity, found by search and listed by explore_file. Indexing reads each repository's application* / bootstrap* configuration for base URLs, service names and context paths, and recomputes the links across all repositories after every run, so they do not depend on indexing order.

Overload addressing (knot 1.14.0). entity=com.x.Foo.bar(int, int) resolves a single overload; resolution.overload reports the parameter list, whether it matched and, when it did not, the declared overloads. Query-side only, no re-index needed.

Untyped receivers (knot 1.14.0, Java/Kotlin). A call on a receiver of unknown type binds by name alone only to a method whose type is visible from the caller's file, and var x = new Foo() types the receiver.

entries.title: Class members no longer take the decorators of an earlier member (#47)
entries.summary: tree-sitter-typescript emits member decorators as siblings in class_body, and the fallback scanned the class body forwards from its first child, so every member after the first decorated one reported…
highlights: Class members no longer take the decorators of an earlier member (#47). tree-sitter-typescript emits member decorators as siblings in class_body, and the fallback scanned the class body forwards from its first child, so every member after the first decorated one reported that member's decorators (plain, reset and update all showed @computed in a MobX store). The scan now walks backwards from the member, collecting only the contiguous decorators written directly before it, skipping comments and anonymous tokens (so @Component(...) export class X keeps its decorators) and stopping at any other node. explore_file, search and the stored decorators field are corrected for decorator-heavy classes (MobX stores, Angular components, NestJS controllers).

TypeScript E2E test 22 (fixture testing_files/typescript/decorators/cart.store.ts) checks per-member decorators through CLI and MCP. Unit tests cover per-member decorators on the TypeScript and TSX grammars (including a comment between decorators) and decorators before export class.

Build the aarch64-apple-darwin release artifact on macos-15. dist 0.31 defaults to macos-14, whose runner image GitHub retires on 2026-11-02; its brownout failed the v1.12.3 release, so v1.12.3 has no GitHub Release binaries (it is on crates.io).
Re-index TypeScript repositories with knot-indexer --clean to correct the stored decorators.

entries.title: Upgrade knot to 1.12.2
entries.summary: Updated the knot dependency from 1.12.1 to 1.12.2.
highlights: Upgrade knot to 1.12.2. Updated the knot dependency from 1.12.1 to 1.12.2. Upstream, Groovy calls whose only argument is a trailing closure (both receiver calls like parts.each { ... } and bare DSL-style calls like withLock { ... }) are now detected and produce a CALLS intent with arity one, so repository methods invoked only through this syntax no longer look unused to find_callers. No API changes required. Re-index Groovy repositories to add the missing CALLS edges.
